profiles.name: Perry Como
profiles.excerpt: Perry Como made radio one of the foundations of a half-century singing career, carrying his relaxed baritone from big-band broadcasting to records and television.
profiles.bio_html:
Perry Como was born Pierino Ronald Como in Canonsburg, Pennsylvania in 1912. He worked as a barber before leaving the trade to sing professionally, first with Freddie Carlone and then with Ted Weems. By the early 1940s, radio and recording had turned his easy baritone into a national sound.

Como became a major radio musical personality through programs including The Chesterfield Supper Club, then carried the same understated style into television and a long recording career with RCA Victor. His occasional acting does not change the center of that career: he was first and foremost one of American popular music's defining vocalists.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 18 Fibber McGee and Molly broadcasts featuring Como, plus appearances on Mr. Keen, Tracer of Lost Persons and The Big Show. Those credits are best understood as appearances by a major singer and radio personality rather than as an actor-primary repertory career.
